claims.text: (TaNb)0.67(HfZrTi)0.33 has a body-centered-cubic structure at ambient pressure.
The HEA's superconductivity remains robust under very high pressure.
The zero-resistance superconducting state of (TaNb)0.67(HfZrTi)0.33 persists to approximately 190 GPa.
The intrinsic stability of the disordered bcc lattice governs the HEA's robust superconductivity.
High configurational entropy stabilizes the HEA's bcc phase against pressure-induced lattice distortions.
The HEA maintains an intact disordered bcc lattice across the investigated pressure range.
Pressure-resistant bcc structural stability prevents significant changes in the electronic density of states relevant to Cooper pairing.
Pressure-resistant bcc structural stability preserves or enhances superconducting pairing interactions.
Under increasing pressure, the HEA's transition temperature will remain relatively stable or increase relative to its ambient-pressure value.
The pressure dependence of Tc in the HEA will be more robust than in elemental Nb or Ta.
Elemental Nb or Ta will likely show decreasing Tc under pressure.
Pressure typically modifies superconducting pairing interactions more drastically in pure bcc metals than in the HEA.
Elemental Nb and Ta are appropriate pure conventional bcc-superconductor baselines for isolating the effect attributed to HEA disorder and mixing entropy.
The proposed mechanism applies only while the HEA remains chemically homogeneous and retains its bcc phase.
Minor phase segregation or unrecognized inhomogeneity could affect the observed pressure dependence of superconductivity.

contradictions.description: Loss of the bcc phase is defined both as outside the hypothesis's stated domain and as a result that falsifies the hypothesis. A phase transition would therefore be ambiguous between boundary-condition failure and mechanistic falsification.
